name: Qian Liang
categoryNote: Chinese 黑茶, “black tea”, is not English black tea (红茶). Puer’s relationship to the dark class is contested; this atlas files it here by process.
pluckStandard: coarse leaf steamed and packed into a bamboo log

transformation.note: Anhua hei cha compressed as a 花卷 log. Microbial change in the column, not a light oolong at oxidation 18, and not 渥堆 in the puer sense.

processing.description: Dark-tea sha qing on Hunan leaf; this is 黑茶 as a class, not a translation problem.
Maocha rolled, then gathered for the log.
Steamed and packed into bamboo and palm-leaf as 花卷. The “thousand taels” is a traditional size of that column, not a tasting note.
Slow microbial change inside the wrapped column. Related to Anhua hei cha and Fu brick, not a shortcut wo dui.

profile.mouthfeel: thick, low bitterness, built for a long session or a boil

rinses.notes: rinse the broken log; the first water is not a cup

decoction.when: after the gongfu session, or as a separate pot
decoction.notes: 煮茶 — simmer the spent log. Dark teas can take a boil; this is the extra cup the name 第四泡 points at.

water.note: Boiling, mineral water is comfortable. A frontier tea built for frontier water.

storage: Dry, whole logs or well-wrapped chunks. Damp storage is mould, not “camphor”.

shelfLife.note: Most teas are food. A few teas are projects.

qualityMarkers.claim: bamboo-wrapped log or a clearly cut slice

commonFaults.name: confused with Fu brick golden flowers

compare.differentiator: Same Anhua dark-tea family. Fu brick is flowered; Qian Liang is the bamboo log. Neither is puer.

summary: Anhua’s bamboo-log dark tea: thousand-tael 花卷, grain-jujube depth, a boil at the end of the session.

photo.alt: Second infusion of Anhua dark tea
photo.caption: Anhua dark-tea liquor. Qian Liang is the thousand-tael log of the same Hunan heicha tradition.
